A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title and substantial reorganization. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V1 reports original cross-modal transfer experiments on three VLMs, LLM-to-VLM transfer, instruction ensembling, and analyses of internal representations, including appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds VQA transfer results, quantitative task-overriding evaluations, computational measurements, and instruction-noise experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions extract task activations at a delimiter token, patch them into a selected layer for another query, and average instruction- and example-derived vectors for ensembling. V2 reformulates the explanation and notation; the added evaluations do not establish a changed extraction, patching, or ensembling procedure.

E1.justification: V2 extends the six constructed tasks with Food-Class, Shirt-Color, and Man-Holding tasks from VQAv2, using LLaVA-ReCap descriptions as textual counterparts. It expands task-conflict coverage to semantic, formatting, creative-generation, and factual-recall scenarios, including OK-VQA/A-OKVQA, and evaluates typo-corrupted instructions. Earlier image-to-text examples remain in Appendix A.7.

E2.justification: The main comparator set is retained under Prompt/Patch terminology. V2 adds an explicit system-prompt comparator for task overriding in Table 5 and adds Image Examples Patch to the model-specific template comparison in Table 10; that row was absent from v1 Table 6.

E3.justification: New protocols include question-stratified VQA evaluation, 1000 samples for each of three overriding settings, and 148 factual-recall images. Overriding uses GPT4o to judge attempted task adherence, counting responses addressing both tasks as successes. V2 also introduces character-swap corruption and timing with 30 examples. The original six-task splits, five-example setup, models, and first-token accuracy metric remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds instruction-typo robustness and computational-overhead analyses, substantially expands task-conflict testing, and compares context embeddings against task vectors. It replaces v1's multi-layer t-SNE sweep with this single-layer comparison and removes the car-manufacturer overriding failure example. Existing template, modality-combination, and representation-evolution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly reports three-seed averaging and identifies the ensemble plot's shaded regions as variance across those seeds. It also states that timing measurements average 100 runs. V1 already displayed variability and reported aggregation over 100 example sets for representation analyses; the new disclosures do not establish increased run counts for retained experiments.

E6.justification: The matched main transfer, LLM-to-VLM, and modality-combination tables retain identical numerical entries. Substantial new results include VQA average accuracy of 0.69 for text patching versus 0.63 for text prompting and 0.52 for image prompting, overriding scores, timing/VRAM measurements, and noisy-instruction averages of 0.39, 0.37, and 0.35. The template ablation gains an image-patching row averaging 0.22.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. V2's patching equation restates the existing extraction-and-application mapping. Its softmax and logit-lens pseudocode explains an existing visualization rather than introducing a new mathematical result or demonstrated change in its definition.

C1.justification: The central claim of shared cross-modal task representations remains. V2 adds the explicit claim that task-level sharing coexists with modality-specific context embeddings and describes compressed-vector superiority over full prompting as peculiar to the cross-modal case. LLM-to-VLM transfer and instruction-derived vectors receive greater prominence but were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 develops a substantive distinction between modality-specific context embeddings and integration within task vectors. It replaces the out-of-domain explanation for prompting failures with an ignored-prefix/forced-application interpretation and explains stronger syntax prompting through potentially compatible instructions. Conversely, it removes the explicit harder-task overriding failure qualification. Image-to-text weaknesses remain discussed in the appendix.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands documentation through the overriding evaluator prompt and success rule, task pools, VQA construction details, visualization pseudocode, and t-SNE normalization/sampling instructions. It also drops explicitly listed optimal layer indices and changes the stated Animal-Latin label source from iNaturalist 2017 to 2021; the PDFs do not establish whether the evaluated samples changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds connections to simplicity bias, cross-modal few-shot learning, in-context vectors, and modality separation, alongside references supporting the new evaluations. Its Lin et al. citation now identifies cross-modal few-shot learning rather than the earlier VILA paper. These changes broaden the context while preserving the central positioning around cross-modal task vectors.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and much explanatory prose are rewritten. Related work moves near the beginning, representation evolution follows the experiments, and image-to-text transfer moves into the appendix. Terminology changes from ICL/Base/xPatch to Examples/Prompt/Patch, with reorganized experimental subsections, explicit findings, and a new impact statement.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the conceptual and patching diagrams, introduces finding boxes and new experimental tables, and adds evaluator-prompt and pseudocode figures. It reorganizes retained displays, adds a cross-modality column to the main results table, replaces the multi-layer t-SNE figure, and removes the standalone instruction examples and one overriding example.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence beyond v1's constructed task suite and qualitative overriding examples through VQA transfer, controlled overriding comparisons, and robustness and efficiency analyses. Seed reporting, evaluator instructions, and visualization pseudocode improve auditability. Removing the overriding failure example and multi-layer t-SNE sweep reduces some transparency, and the new overriding scores measure attempted adherence rather than answer correctness. Nevertheless, the broader validation and clearer documentation substantially improve the paper's evidential support and assessability.
